text: A short lesson for creative-workshop facilitators.
Write a task that names an observable action, the material and the evidence of completion.
12 minutes planned / no design training needed
ORIGINAL TEACHING EXAMPLE / no observed learner results
You will rewrite a request. A partner will check it using the same three criteria.
Write or dictate. A partner may mark the choice and record your exact words.
Planned timing only. Pause or extend when a learner needs it.
ORIGINAL TEACHING EXAMPLE / no observed learner results
What would a partner do first? How would you know they finished?
A / Repair together B / Fix and learn C / Second life D / Skill swap
The job: choose one option and give one reason.
ORIGINAL TEACHING EXAMPLE / no observed learner results
Circle one title card from A–D.
The choice is visible. Where will the reason appear?
ORIGINAL TEACHING EXAMPLE / no observed learner results
Circle one title card from A–D. Write one reason for your choice.
A partner can check both parts. A clear task still needs a real trial.
ORIGINAL TEACHING EXAMPLE / no observed learner results
Rewrite “Review these headlines.” Request one choice and one recorded reason.
1 / Make space 2 / Share a skill 3 / Try it together 4 / Bring a question
[Write, dictate or rehearse your wording here.]
Check action, material and completion evidence.
ORIGINAL TEACHING EXAMPLE / no observed learner results
Underline one headline from 1–4. Write one reason for your choice.
One possible response. Different wording can meet the same criteria.
Name one phrase that meets a criterion. Ask for the missing evidence, then rewrite.
ORIGINAL TEACHING EXAMPLE / no observed learner results
Write a task for choosing one workshop activity. Require one choice and one recorded reason.
A / Paper collage B / Story circle C / Object drawing
A partner checks all three criteria. Revise any missing part.
ORIGINAL TEACHING EXAMPLE / no observed learner results
Ready for a real trial when all three criteria are Met.
Keep the instruction and your partner’s criterion notes. Mark each criterion Met or Revise.
This exercise checks the wording. It does not prove that a real group will succeed.
Next: try the instruction with your intended group and record what they do.
ORIGINAL TEACHING EXAMPLE / no observed learner results
